title: Structured Markdown Plugin Output Contract (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose

Quick personal scratchpad for a narrow API/contract to surface plugin/tool results as structured Markdown that the host (UI/client/runtime) can render deterministically, apply incremental updates, and validate for safety without needing to fully parse arbitrary HTML. Trying to design something minimal, streaming-friendly, and friendly to diffs/patches.

Goals / constraints
- Output should be valid Markdown-ish (subset) with explicit block semantics so renderers can choose richer widgets or fallback to plain text.
- Support streaming partial updates (append / replace / patch operations).
- Include light rendering hints (role, intent) but no executable code.
- Include provenance & verification metadata for auditability (plugin id, signature stub, version).
- Keep it backwards compatible with simple text output: renderer can drop structured fields and still display readable Markdown.
- Allow plugins to suggest interactive widgets (e.g., calendar card) but host has final say — only hinting, not executable.

High-level shape (informal)
- Top-level object: { plugin_id, invocation_id, result_id, status, structured_markdown, metadata }
- structured_markdown: array of top-level blocks (ordered)
- Block types: paragraph, heading, list, code, table, block_quote, callout, card, attach (for attachments), diff (for patch ops)
- Each block: { type, id?, text?, attrs? } where attrs are conservative rendering hints (map of string->string)

Example (single-response)

{
  "plugin_id": "calendar.v1",
  "invocation_id": "inv-20260310-9f2b",
  "result_id": "r-7c3d",
  "status": "ok",
  "structured_markdown": [
    { "type": "heading", "text": "Meeting summary" },
    { "type": "paragraph", "text": "We scheduled a sync for Tuesday 9am PT. Participants: Ana, Marco, Priya." },
    { "type": "callout", "attrs": { "intent": "action-item", "severity": "info" }, "text": "Priya to share agenda by Monday EOD." },
    { "type": "card", "attrs": { "card_type": "calendar-event", "event_id": "ev-3342" }, "text": "" }
  ],
  "metadata": { "plugin_version": "1.0.3", "signed_by": "plugin@calendar", "signature_stub": "sig:abc..." }
}

Notes on the example:
- "card" block: renderer can choose to show an interactive calendar widget or render a compact markdown fallback. The card block must include enough id/attrs to allow the host to fetch a safe representation if needed.
- signature_stub is deliberately short; full verification flows are out-of-scope for this draft but placeholder included so audit logs can point to verification artifacts.

Block semantics and allowed content (brainstorm)
- paragraph: plain markdown text (no raw HTML), may include inline links.
- heading: text, attrs.level: 1..6 optional.
- list: attrs.ordered=true/false, items: array of strings (or nested blocks allowed optionally).
- code: attrs.lang optional; text is code fence.
- table: simple row/column array (limit widths).
- callout: short single paragraph with attrs.intent (note/warning/action) and maybe ttl.
- card: attrs.card_type canonicalized (calendar-event, file-preview, map) + id. Renderer should not execute scripts from card payloads.
- attach: file reference: attrs.mime, attrs.preview_url (host may fetch via signed url).
- diff: used for streaming/patching, see patching below.

Streaming / patch model (rough)
- For long responses or incremental tool invocations we use op-style patches. Patch blocks have type: diff and attrs: { op: "append" | "replace" | "insert_after:block_id" | "delete:block_id" }
- Each diff contains a small structured_markdown fragment. Example streaming chunk:

{ "type": "diff", "attrs": { "op": "append" }, "text": "\\n- partial result line 1\\n- partial result line 2" }

- Each patch must include invocation_id + sequence integer in outer metadata so host can re-order/chunk and detect missing pieces.

Rendering hints (attrs) — conservative list
- intent: (info, warning, action, meta)
- role: (assistant, plugin, user) — helps attribution UI
- card_type: string (canonical)
- provenance_id: string (link into audit logs)
- suggested_fallback: (markdown | plain_text)

Safety rules (host responsibility)
- No raw HTML or script allowed in text fields. Only a small safe subset of Markdown: emphasis, links, code fences, lists, blockquotes, headings, tables (simple).
- Renderer must strip any suspicious unicode control chars.
- Attach/card payloads must be fetched through host-provided signed URLs or validated content proxies.
- Plugins must declare when content is generated from user data or third-party sources (attrs.source_hint).

Backward compatibility and simple clients
- Simple clients that only display a blob of text should join block.text fields with double newlines and ignore attrs. That produces a readable plain fallback.
- If structured_markdown missing, fallback to raw_text field if present.

Example: minimal backward-compatible blob

{
  "plugin_id": "weather.v1",
  "invocation_id": "inv-xx",
  "status": "ok",
  "raw_text": "Sunny. High 65F. Low 48F."
}

Patch compatibility / merging rules
- Host maintains canonical block id ordering. Each block may optionally include an id (client-supplied or server-generated).
- Replace/insert operations reference block ids; append doesn't need ids.
- If host detects conflicting replace for same block_id from different sequences, prefer the highest-sequence number unless signatures indicate otherwise.

Telemetry / cost considerations (notes to self)
- Keep block granularity coarse to avoid token explosion in small edits. Use "diff" op sparingly.
- Instrument counts: blocks emitted, patch ops, attach sizes. Useful for Optimize tool recommendations.

UI affordances to support
- Inline provenance hover (who produced this paragraph, tool + confidence)
- Collapse/expand cards and heavy attachments
- Attribution control: hide plugin attribution until user expands (for lower-trust plugins)

Example ASCII flow diagram (very rough)

Client UI <--(stream chunks)-- Redwood runtime <--(plugin invocation via sandbox API)-- Plugin process
            |                                   |-- verifies signature? --|
            |-- render blocks & show cards --> display / fetch attachments via host proxy

Open questions / TODOs
- Tie-in with existing function-calling output schema: can we reuse that for structured_markdown blocks? Avoid two competing shapes.
- Should signature verification be mandatory for card blocks that carry external fetch URLs? Probably yes.
- Do we allow nested blocks (e.g., lists with sub-blocks)? Simpler to start with arrays of shallow blocks.
- How to express inline variables / placeholders that host can substitute safely? Need placeholder syntax and allowed token types.
- Consider a tiny JSON Schema for block attrs so plugin authors have quick linting.

Implementation notes (personal checklist)
- [ ] Draft lightweight JSON Schema (blocks + top-level).
- [ ] Proto compatibility sketch for streaming (sequence ids, checksums).
- [ ] Try a minimal host renderer that concatenates text fallback and special-cases callout & card.
- [ ] Talk to SDK team about serialization helpers (builders for plugin authors).

Rough JSON Schema idea (text only — for later)
- top-level: plugin_id (string), invocation_id (string), status (enum), structured_markdown (array of block objects), raw_text optional, metadata optional
- block object: type (enum), id optional, text optional, attrs optional (map string->string)

Closing note
This is intentionally fuzzy — aim is to converge on a small, conservative contract that gives clients enough structure to build deterministic renderers while keeping plugin authors’ surface area small. Will iterate with SDK and UI folks once I have a small schema and a tiny reference renderer.

End of scratchpad.
